## Fs

Capability: `fileio`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fs.write(path: string, data: string) -> bool` | `fileio` | Sandboxed file store. A script gets its own directory and nothing else: a path is validated before use (no absolute path, no backslash, no drive letter, no control character, no empty segment, no \".\" or \"..\", a bounded length and depth), so a path cannot escape the sandbox however it is spelled. Writes are capped per file, in total and in count, so a write loop cannot exhaust memory. Every call fails closed (false / empty) rather than throwing. When the embedder configures a script data directory, the store persists to a per-script directory there: every path component is opened without following a symlink, a write lands in a temporary file that is renamed into place (so a reader never sees a partial write), and the existing files and bytes are counted against the quota when the directory is opened, so data survives a restart and a planted symlink or a traversal spelling is refused. |
| `fs.read(path: string) -> string` | `fileio` | - |
| `fs.append(path: string, data: string) -> bool` | `fileio` | - |
| `fs.exists(path: string) -> bool` | `fileio` | - |
| `fs.remove(path: string) -> bool` | `fileio` | - |
| `fs.size(path: string) -> number` | `fileio` | - |
| `fs.list(prefix: string) -> string` | `fileio` | Every path in the sandbox, sorted, newline-separated. `prefix` filters to paths that start with it; an empty prefix lists everything. |
| `fs.count() -> number` | `fileio` | - |
| `fs.total_bytes() -> number` | `fileio` | - |
| `fs.clear() -> nil` | `fileio` | - |

## Packets

Capability: `packets`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packets.recent(max: number) -> Table` | `packets` | Read-only packet inspection. The log holds packet METADATA only — a sequence number, direction, protocol id, a name and a byte length — and never payload bytes, so it cannot become a collection surface. It answers the diagnostic questions (am I being spammed, is this id new since the update, how much am I sending) without exposing anyone's data. Fed by the network layer; a script only reads it. `recent` returns a table keyed \"0\",\"1\",…, newest first, each {seq, dir, id, name, bytes, time_ms}; `summary` is the same shape per id, highest count first. `dir` is \"inbound\", \"outbound\" or \"\" for both. |

## Network

Capability: `network`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `network.get(url: string, timeout_ms: number) -> HttpResult` | `network` | Outbound requests. Requires a network grant scoped to the host. Both calls return an HttpResult table (status, ok, headers, body, error, truncated) rather than raising, so a script can branch on the outcome; headers is a newline-separated \"Name: value\" list. A refused destination (bad URL, egress policy, or a host outside the grant) comes back with status 0 and a non-empty error. TLS is not implemented, so an https destination is refused rather than downgraded to plaintext. |
| `network.post(url: string, body: string, timeout_ms: number) -> HttpResult` | `network` | - |

## Ws

Capability: `network`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws.connect(url: string, timeout_ms: number) -> number` | `network` | WebSocket client. Requires a network grant scoped to the host, and the same egress policy `network.get` uses: a ws:// URL to a private or reserved host is refused, and wss:// fails closed because TLS is not implemented. A connection is addressed by an integer handle; the frames a peer sends are buffered in order and read with `ws.poll` after `ws.pump`. Every call runs on the script worker (blocking reads are expected there). `ws.connect` returns 0 and raises on a refused destination or a failed handshake. `ws.poll` returns {ok, opcode, data, binary}; `ok` is false when the inbox is empty. |

## JsonRpc

Capability: `network`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `json_rpc.call(url: string, method: string, params_json: string, timeout_ms: number) -> Table` | `network` | JSON-RPC 2.0 client. Issues one call over the same egress-checked HTTP path as `network.post`, so the destination rules are identical. The response is validated as JSON-RPC 2.0 and its id must match before the result is trusted. `call` returns {ok, result, error_code, error_message, status}: `result` is a structured table decoded from the reply's `result` member, and a transport failure (bad URL, refused destination, HTTP status, malformed envelope) comes back with `ok` false and `error_message` set, so a script branches on the outcome rather than unwinding. `params_json` is raw JSON (an object or array); an empty string omits `params`. |

## Perf

Capability: `perf`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `perf.frame_time_ms() -> number` | `perf` | Frame timing and quality controls. |
| `perf.stats() -> Table` | `perf` | - |
| `perf.quality() -> number` | `perf` | - |
| `perf.set_target_fps(fps: number) -> nil` | `perf` | - |
| `perf.set_thermal_mode(enabled: bool) -> nil` | `perf` | - |
| `perf.set_platform(name: string) -> nil` | `perf` | Select the device profile the governor tunes itself for: generic, mobile-low, mobile-high or desktop. Unknown names are refused (fail closed). |
| `perf.flame() -> Table` | `perf` | The aggregated span call tree since the last `perf.flame_reset`, as a nested table: each node is {name, self_ms, total_ms, count, children}, and `children` is ordered by total time descending so the expensive branch reads first. `self_ms` excludes child spans, so a parent's `total_ms` is the time actually spent inside it. Populated by the profiler spans the modules and hooks raise. |
| `perf.spans() -> Table` | `perf` | The flat span list, highest total time first: a table keyed \"0\",\"1\",… each {name, total_ms, count, max_ms}. The list view of the same data `flame` nests. |
| `perf.flame_reset() -> nil` | `perf` | Drops the flame tree, the span stats and the per-frame ring, starting the profiler over. |
| `perf.pipeline() -> Table` | `perf` | The render pipeline's frame counters as {frames, entities_submitted, entities_drawn, entities_culled, entities_lod_reduced, batches, draw_calls, vertices, resolution_scale}. `draw_calls` counts the two coalesced calls (triangles + lines) a frame issues, so it stays flat however many primitives a script queued; `resolution_scale` is the factor the dynamic-resolution controller settled on (1.0 is native). |
| `perf.lod_tier(distance: number) -> string` | `perf` | The level-of-detail tier an entity `distance` blocks from the camera would be drawn at: \"full\", \"reduced\", \"static\" or \"culled\". Follows the same policy the renderer culls with, so a script can predict whether its overlay will be given geometry. |
| `perf.lod_should_tick(distance: number, tick: number, phase: number) -> bool` | `perf` | Whether an entity `distance` blocks away should advance its animation/physics on `tick`, keyed by `phase` (pass the entity id so a crowd does not all update on one tick). True every tick at \"full\", one tick in the policy's reduced interval at \"reduced\", never at \"static\"/\"culled\". This is the tick-rate half of LOD: a script that drives a crowd skips a false result to throttle it. |

## Events

Capability: `events`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `events.on(channel: string, handler: string) -> number` | `events` | Registers `handler` (a function exported by the script) on `channel`. Returns a subscription id, or 0 when refused (empty/oversized channel or handler name, unknown channel, or the subscription cap is reached). The handler is called with the payload as its first argument; a channel with no payload delivers an empty string. Re-registering the same (channel, handler) pair returns the existing id rather than adding a duplicate. |
| `events.off(id: number) -> bool` | `events` | Removes the subscription with `id`. Returns true when one was removed. |
| `events.off_all() -> number` | `events` | Removes every subscription the calling script holds. Returns how many were removed. |
| `events.subscriptions() -> number` | `events` | How many subscriptions the calling script holds. |
| `events.emit(channel: string, payload: string) -> number` | `events` | Publishes `payload` on `channel` to every subscriber (this script included, unless it has no subscription). Returns how many handlers were dispatched. An empty or oversized channel is refused (returns 0). |
| `events.channels() -> string` | `events` | The declared channels and every channel a script has subscribed to, comma-separated and sorted, so a script can discover what it can listen for. |

Events (await with `Events.once`):

- `hit(damage: number)` — -
- `kill(victim: string)` — -
- `tick_count(count: number)` — -
- `entityEntered(entity: string)` — -
- `entityLeft(entity: string)` — -
- `entityUpdated(entity: string)` — -
- `blockChanged(change: string)` — -
- `entityHurt(entity: string)` — -
- `entityDeath(entity: string)` — -
- `entitySpawn(entity: string)` — -
- `combatPredicted(hit: string)` — A hit the local client predicted (the swing it believes will land). Carries \"<attacker>:<victim>\".
- `combatConfirmed(hit: string)` — A predicted hit the engine then confirmed. Carries \"<attacker>:<victim>\".
- `combatMissed(hit: string)` — A predicted hit that was never confirmed within the prediction window. Carries \"<attacker>:<victim>\".
- `radialSelected(label: string)` — The label of the radial-menu item the player committed, fired once on the release that selects it.
- `crystalAdvice(placement: string)` — The best crystal placement changed while the advisor is armed. Carries \"x,y,z,score\".

| `package.add(manifest_json: string) -> bool` | `fileio` | Script package registry and resolver. A package is a JSON manifest plus an entry file; a script declares dependencies with version constraints. | `radial.add_item(label: string, enabled: bool) -> bool` | `hud` | Appends an item. False when the label is empty, longer than 32 bytes or non-printable, or the menu already holds its maximum of 12 items. |
| `radial.remove_item(index: number) -> bool` | `hud` | Removes the item at `index`. False when out of range. |
| `radial.clear() -> nil` | `hud` | Removes every item and closes the menu. |
| `radial.count() -> number` | `hud` | How many items the menu holds. |
| `radial.item_label(index: number) -> string` | `hud` | The label at `index`, or an empty string when out of range. |
| `radial.item_enabled(index: number) -> bool` | `hud` | Whether the item at `index` is enabled; false when out of range. |
| `radial.set_item_enabled(index: number, enabled: bool) -> bool` | `hud` | Enables or disables an item. False when out of range. |
| `radial.open() -> bool` | `hud` | Opens the menu. False when it holds no items (an empty menu is not worth showing) or is already open. |
| `radial.close() -> nil` | `hud` | Closes the menu and clears the hover and selection. |
| `radial.is_open() -> bool` | `hud` | True while the menu is open. |
| `radial.radius() -> number` | `hud` | The outer radius in pixels. |
| `radial.set_radius(radius: number) -> bool` | `hud` | Sets the outer radius. Must be finite and positive and greater than the inner radius; a bad value is refused. |
| `radial.inner_radius() -> number` | `hud` | The inner (dead-zone) radius in pixels. |
| `radial.set_inner_radius(radius: number) -> bool` | `hud` | Sets the inner radius. Must be finite, non-negative and less than the outer radius; a bad value is refused. |
| `radial.open_ms() -> number` | `hud` | The open/close animation duration in milliseconds. |
| `radial.set_open_ms(ms: number) -> bool` | `hud` | Sets the open animation duration. Must be finite and positive; a bad value is refused. |
| `radial.state() -> Table` | `hud` | The current menu state as {open, hovered, selected, progress, items}. `hovered`/`selected` are -1 when none. |
| `radial.sector_at(pointer_x: number, pointer_y: number, center_x: number, center_y: number, inner_radius: number, outer_radius: number, count: number) -> number` | `hud` | The sector under a pointer relative to a centre for `count` sectors, or -1 for the dead zone or outside the ring. Pure: it reads no state, so it pins the geometry. |

## Touch

Capability: `input`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `touch.pointer_down(id: number, x: number, y: number, now_ms: number) -> bool` | `input` | Records a finger going down at (x, y) with the engine's finger id. False when the pointer table (10 fingers) is full. |
| `touch.pointer_move(id: number, x: number, y: number, now_ms: number) -> nil` | `input` | Records a finger moving. Ignored when the id is not down. |
| `touch.pointer_up(id: number, x: number, y: number, now_ms: number) -> nil` | `input` | Records a finger lifting and resolves the single-finger gesture (tap, double tap or swipe) it completes. |
| `touch.clear_pointers() -> nil` | `input` | Drops every pointer, e.g. on a focus loss or screen change. |
| `touch.pointer_count() -> number` | `input` | How many fingers are down. |
| `touch.pointers() -> Table` | `input` | The fingers currently down, oldest first, as a table keyed \"0\",\"1\",… of {id, x, y, start_x, start_y, down_ms}. |
| `touch.update(now_ms: number) -> nil` | `input` | Advances the recogniser (long press, drag, pinch, rotate) and hit-tests the on-screen buttons against the primary finger for this frame. |
| `touch.set_gesture_enabled(gesture: string, enabled: bool) -> bool` | `input` | Enables or disables one gesture (by name: tap, double_tap, long_press, drag, swipe, pinch, rotate). False for an unknown name. |
| `touch.gesture_enabled(gesture: string) -> bool` | `input` | Whether a gesture is enabled. False for an unknown name. |
| `touch.gesture_mask() -> number` | `input` | The enabled-gesture mask as a bit set (tap=1, double_tap=2, long_press=4, drag=8, swipe=16, pinch=32, rotate=64). |
| `touch.last_gesture() -> Table` | `input` | The last recognised gesture as {kind, dir, x, y, dx, dy, magnitude, pointers, at_ms}. `kind` is \"none\" before any gesture. |
| `touch.config() -> Table` | `input` | The recogniser thresholds as {tap_max_move, tap_max_ms, long_press_ms, double_tap_max_ms, swipe_min_dist, swipe_max_ms, pinch_min_scale}. |
| `touch.set_tap_max_move(px: number) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the movement that still counts as a tap, in pixels. Must be finite and positive; a bad value is refused. |
| `touch.set_tap_max_ms(ms: number) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the duration that still counts as a tap, in milliseconds. Must be finite and positive. |
| `touch.set_long_press_ms(ms: number) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the hold time before a long press fires, in milliseconds. Must be finite and positive. |
| `touch.set_double_tap_max_ms(ms: number) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the window for a second tap to become a double tap, in milliseconds. Must be finite and positive. |
| `touch.set_swipe_min_dist(px: number) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the travel that makes a release a swipe, in pixels. Must be finite and positive. |
| `touch.set_swipe_max_ms(ms: number) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the maximum duration of a swipe, in milliseconds. Must be finite and positive. |
| `touch.set_pinch_min_scale(scale: number) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the separation change that fires a pinch, as a scale fraction. Must be finite, positive and at most 1. |
| `touch.swipe_direction(dx: number, dy: number, min_dist: number) -> string` | `input` | The direction a swipe of (dx, dy) travels — up, down, left or right — or \"none\" when it is shorter than `min_dist`. Pure: it reads no state, so it pins the geometry. |
| `touch.add_button(label: string, min_x: number, min_y: number, max_x: number, max_y: number) -> bool` | `input` | Adds an on-screen button covering (min_x, min_y)..(max_x, max_y). False when the label is empty, longer than 24 bytes or non-printable, the rectangle is not finite or not positive-area, or the button cap (24) is reached. |
| `touch.remove_button(index: number) -> bool` | `input` | Removes the button at `index`. False when out of range. |
| `touch.clear_buttons() -> nil` | `input` | Removes every button. |
| `touch.button_count() -> number` | `input` | How many buttons exist. |
| `touch.button_label(index: number) -> string` | `input` | The label at `index`, or an empty string when out of range. |
| `touch.button_enabled(index: number) -> bool` | `input` | Whether the button at `index` is enabled; false when out of range. |
| `touch.set_button_enabled(index: number, enabled: bool) -> bool` | `input` | Enables or disables the button at `index`. False when out of range. |
| `touch.set_button_intent(index: number, intent: string) -> bool` | `input` | Sets the intent the button requests on press (an intent name such as \"zoom\"; empty clears it). False when out of range or the name is not a bounded identifier. |
| `touch.button_intent(index: number) -> string` | `input` | The intent the button at `index` requests, or an empty string. |
| `touch.button_state(index: number) -> Table` | `input` | A snapshot of the button at `index` as {label, enabled, held, toggled, allowed, presses, releases}. `allowed` is false when the button's intent is refused by this server's policy. |
| `touch.state() -> Table` | `input` | The overall touch state as {pointers, buttons, gesture}. `gesture` is the last gesture table. |

Events (await with `Events.once`):

- `touchGesture(gesture: string)` — -

## Crystal

Capability: `crystal`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crystal.config() -> Table` | `crystal` | The current tunables as {place_range, blast_radius, max_damage, min_targets, self_damage_weight, max_self_damage, levels, max_results}. |
| `crystal.set_range(range: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets the placement range in blocks. Must be finite, positive and at most 16; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.set_blast_radius(radius: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets the blast radius in blocks. Must be finite, positive and at most 32; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.set_max_damage(damage: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets the damage at the epicentre before falloff. Must be finite and non-negative; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.set_min_targets(n: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets the minimum number of targets a spot must hit to be recommended. Must be a non-negative integer; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.set_self_damage_weight(weight: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets how heavily damage to the placer is weighted against damage to enemies. Must be finite and non-negative; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.set_max_self_damage(damage: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets the most damage a recommended spot may deal to the placer. Must be finite and non-negative; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.set_levels(levels: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets the number of block levels above and below the placer's feet to consider. Must be an integer in [0, 4]; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.set_max_results(n: number) -> bool` | `crystal` | Sets how many recommendations an analysis keeps. Must be an integer in [1, 4096]; a bad value is refused. |
| `crystal.analyze(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> number` | `crystal` | Ranks the candidate placements around a placer at (x, y, z) against the entities the world grid already read, and returns how many were recommended. Fails closed (returns 0) when the world or the advisor is unavailable. The ranking is available through `count` and `placement`. |
| `crystal.count() -> number` | `crystal` | How many recommendations the last analysis produced. |
| `crystal.best() -> Table` | `crystal` | The best recommendation as {ok, x, y, z, targets, total_damage, best_damage, self_damage, score}. `ok` is false when there is none. |
| `crystal.placement(index: number) -> Table` | `crystal` | The recommendation at `index` in the last ranking, same shape as `best`, or an empty table when out of range. |
| `crystal.estimate(x: number, y: number, z: number, tx: number, ty: number, tz: number) -> number` | `crystal` | The estimated damage a blast at (x, y, z) would deal to a target at (tx, ty, tz) under the current tunables. Pure: it reads no world state. |
| `crystal.stats() -> Table` | `crystal` | The advisor's counters as {analyses, candidates, placements, best_score}. |
| `crystal.reset() -> nil` | `crystal` | Forgets the last ranking and its counters. |
| `crystal.arm() -> bool` | `crystal` | Arms the advisor. While armed, the client's tick hook runs one advisory pass per game tick around the local player and fires `crystalAdvice` when the best spot changes. False when it is already armed. |
| `crystal.disarm() -> nil` | `crystal` | Disarms the advisor. A no-op when it is already disarmed. |
| `crystal.armed() -> bool` | `crystal` | True while the advisor runs its advisory pass on the game tick. |

## Voice

Capability: `voice`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `voice.config() -> Table` | `voice` | The current tunables as {max_range, full_volume_range, master_volume, max_speakers, hold_ms, max_frame_bytes, min_send_interval_ms}. |
| `voice.set_max_range(range: number) -> bool` | `voice` | Sets how far a speaker is heard, in blocks. Must be finite and in (0, 128]; a bad value is refused. |
| `voice.set_full_volume_range(range: number) -> bool` | `voice` | Sets the distance within which a speaker plays at full volume. Must be finite and in [0, max_range]; a bad value is refused. |
| `voice.set_master_volume(volume: number) -> bool` | `voice` | Sets the playback master volume. Must be finite and in [0, 1]; a bad value is refused. |
| `voice.set_max_speakers(n: number) -> bool` | `voice` | Sets how many speakers are mixed at once. Must be an integer in [1, 32]; a bad value is refused. |
| `voice.set_hold_ms(ms: number) -> bool` | `voice` | Sets how long a speaker stays listed as talking after its last frame, in ms. Must be a positive integer; a bad value is refused. |
| `voice.set_max_frame_bytes(n: number) -> bool` | `voice` | Sets the largest inbound frame payload accepted, in bytes. Must be an integer in [1, 2048]; a bad value is refused. |
| `voice.set_min_send_interval_ms(ms: number) -> bool` | `voice` | Sets the shortest gap between outgoing frames, in ms. Must be a positive integer; a bad value is refused. |
| `voice.start(self_id: string) -> bool` | `voice` | Starts a session as `self_id`. False when already running, when the id is malformed (empty, over 64 bytes, or carrying a control character), or when no transport is bound (there is nothing to talk over). |
| `voice.stop() -> nil` | `voice` | Stops the session and forgets the speakers. A no-op when not running. |
| `voice.running() -> bool` | `voice` | True while a session is running. |
| `voice.self_id() -> string` | `voice` | The local session id, or \"\" when not running. |
| `voice.set_talking(talking: bool) -> nil` | `voice` | Sets push-to-talk (or open-mic) state. Only a talking, unmuted session sends; the receive half runs either way. |
| `voice.talking() -> bool` | `voice` | True while the local client is sending. |
| `voice.set_muted(muted: bool) -> nil` | `voice` | Sets the microphone mute. A muted session sends nothing. |
| `voice.muted() -> bool` | `voice` | True while the microphone is muted. |
| `voice.set_position(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> nil` | `voice` | Sets the local player's position, used to judge the proximity of what the listener hears. |
| `voice.speaker_count() -> number` | `voice` | How many speakers are currently heard. |
| `voice.speaker(index: number) -> Table` | `voice` | The speaker at `index` in the activity list (loudest first) as {id, level, distance, last_ms}, or an empty table when out of range. |
| `voice.stats() -> Table` | `voice` | The session counters as {frames_captured, frames_sent, frames_received, frames_dropped, frames_played, bytes_sent, bytes_received}. |
| `voice.reset() -> nil` | `voice` | Forgets the speaker state and the counters, keeping the config and the seams. |
| `voice.transport() -> string` | `voice` | The transport's short name (\"lan\" on device, \"\" when none is bound). |

## ReplayMod

Capability: `world`.

| Function | Capability | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `replaymod.capture_start() -> bool` | `world` | Begins a fresh capture, clearing any previous tape. False when already recording. |
| `replaymod.capture_stop() -> bool` | `world` | Ends the capture and keeps the tape. False when not recording. |
| `replaymod.capturing() -> bool` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.section_count() -> number` | `world` | The number of sections on the tape. |
| `replaymod.bytes() -> number` | `world` | The uncompressed payload bytes currently held. |
| `replaymod.first_tick() -> number` | `world` | The first and last tick held, or 0 when empty. |
| `replaymod.last_tick() -> number` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.save() -> string` | `world` | The tape as one binary replay document, ready to save. Returns \"\" on a write error. |
| `replaymod.load(data: string) -> bool` | `world` | Replaces the loaded replay from a binary document. Rejects the whole document on any error (returns false with a reason in `last_error`) and leaves the current replay untouched. |
| `replaymod.loaded() -> bool` | `world` | True when a replay is loaded. |
| `replaymod.unload() -> nil` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.last_error() -> string` | `world` | Why the last `load` failed, or \"\" after a success. |
| `replaymod.loaded_sections() -> number` | `world` | The loaded replay's section count. |
| `replaymod.loaded_first_tick() -> number` | `world` | The loaded replay's first and last tick, or 0 when none. |
| `replaymod.loaded_last_tick() -> number` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.world_entity_count(tick: number) -> number` | `world` | How many entities the reconstructed world holds at `tick`, or 0 when no replay is loaded. |
| `replaymod.world_entity(tick: number, index: number) -> Table` | `world` | The entity at `index` of the reconstructed world at `tick` as {valid, id, type, x, y, z, health, max_health, alive, name}, or an empty table when out of range. |
| `replaymod.world_block(tick: number, x: number, y: number, z: number) -> number` | `world` | The block id at a block coordinate in the reconstructed world at `tick`, or 0 when no replay is loaded. |
| `replaymod.tick_range() -> Table` | `world` | The replay's tick range as {first, last}, or zeros when none. |
| `replaymod.set_review_active(on: bool) -> nil` | `world` | Turns the local review overlay on or off. Off by default. |
| `replaymod.review_active() -> bool` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.review_play() -> bool` | `world` | Starts the review playback from the loaded replay. False when no replay is loaded. |
| `replaymod.review_pause() -> nil` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.review_playing() -> bool` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.review_tick() -> number` | `world` | The tick the review is showing. |
| `replaymod.review_seek(tick: number) -> bool` | `world` | Moves the review to a tick. False when no replay is loaded. |
| `replaymod.review_speed() -> number` | `world` | The playback speed multiplier. Must be finite and in (0, 64]; a bad value is refused. |
| `replaymod.set_review_speed(speed: number) -> bool` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.review_present() -> number` | `world` | Draws the review through the frame's renderer when active; returns how many entities it drew. A no-op (0) when inactive or no replay is loaded. |
| `replaymod.server_start(host: string, port: number) -> bool` | `world` | Binds the loopback playback server to `host:port`. `host` must be a loopback address (\"127.0.0.1\", \"::1\" or \"localhost\"); anything else is refused. A port of 0 asks the OS for a free one, which `server_port` reports. Returns false (with a reason in `last_error`) when the host is not loopback, the socket cannot bind, the loaded replay's protocol version does not match this build, or a live multiplayer session is active (playback never runs alongside a live session). |
| `replaymod.server_stop() -> nil` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.server_running() -> bool` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.server_live_blocked() -> bool` | `world` | True when the live-session guard is holding playback back: a live multiplayer session is active, so the server is neither started nor streaming. |
| `replaymod.server_port() -> number` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.server_client_connected() -> bool` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.server_packets_sent() -> number` | `world` | How many packets the server has sent since a client joined. |
| `replaymod.server_set_paused(paused: bool) -> nil` | `world` | Pauses or resumes the server's stream (the client stays connected). |
| `replaymod.server_paused() -> bool` | `world` | - |
| `replaymod.server_seek(tick: number) -> bool` | `world` | Restarts the stream for the connected client at the nearest keyframe at or before `tick`. False when no client is connected. |
| `replaymod.status() -> string` | `world` | A one-line status: capture state, sections, bytes, whether a replay is loaded, and whether a client is connected. |
